tasks.title: Verify release integrity and reproduction identity
tasks.prompt: A maintainer needs to tell adopters exactly which published release artifacts and source snapshots to reproduce. Verify the supplied offline report against its adjacent checksum and reconcile the release, benchmark implementation and companion Spec identities. Use inspect_repository_file({repository,path}) to obtain the large report's independently fetched raw SHA-256 and byte size without requesting its full text; read the adjacent checksum with read_repository_file({repository,path}). Source inspection is bounded to 2 MiB and the exact supplied file sources. Optional: inspect_release({repository}) and inspect_release_asset({repository,asset_name}) may inspect the published v0.2.0-draft.1 manuscript.pdf only, also within 2 MiB; PDF inspection is not a substitute for the required report digest check. Clearly separate completed byte checks, claims reported by the release documents and anything you cannot verify. Use read_repository_file({repository,path}) for the supplied text sources; the tool returns the fixed ref. Return a JSON report with the useful Markdown in report_markdown (no more than 6000 UTF-8 bytes), plus task_id, conclusion and source citations. This task starts in a fresh context; do not rely on prior task answers or results.
mandatory_deliverables: A release/source identity table with repository, immutable ref, artifact or dependency role, and source citation.
The selected offline report filename, independently fetched raw-byte SHA-256 and byte size, adjacent published checksum, and explicit comparison outcome or inspection failure.
An explanation of which identities must agree and how to interpret different release and measurement identifiers.
A reproduction recommendation and unresolved verification limitations; any optional PDF observation must remain separate from the required source-file check.

tasks.title: Audit the clean-clone maintainer quickstart
tasks.prompt: A new maintainer needs an offline-first installation and reproduction runbook for the pinned public release. Review the quickstart, prerequisites, dependency pins and published clean-clone verification history. Produce ordered instructions with working directories, readiness checks and failure handling, and identify any warranted clarification. Do not claim that you performed a fresh clone, download, test run or replay merely because a published report describes one. Use read_repository_file({repository,path}) for the supplied file sources; the tool returns the fixed ref. Return a JSON report with the useful Markdown in report_markdown (no more than 6000 UTF-8 bytes), plus task_id, conclusion and source citations. This task starts in a fresh context; do not rely on prior task answers or results.
mandatory_deliverables: An ordered command/checklist sequence specifying prerequisites, checkout identity, directory layout and working directory.
A dependency readiness and integrity checklist, including what to do when setup cannot complete.
A source-cited account of what the published verification actually exercised, including retained unsuccessful attempts.
A clear separation between offline reproduction and any separately authorized live operation.
An evidence-based documentation disposition: a precise clarification if warranted, or an explanation that no change is needed.

tasks.title: Prepare the v1 to v1.1 consumer migration note
tasks.prompt: A maintainer is considering offline-consumer-v1.1 while preserving existing offline-consumer-v1 clients. Read the pinned consumer contracts and change record. Prepare an adoption and rollback note covering selection, configuration, externally visible behavior and verification. Keep release, core wire, domain profile and processing-contract identities distinct, and base every claimed behavior change on the supplied sources rather than assuming a version number implies a change. Use read_repository_file({repository,path}) for the supplied file sources; the tool returns the fixed ref. Return a JSON report with the useful Markdown in report_markdown (no more than 6000 UTF-8 bytes), plus task_id, conclusion and source citations. This task starts in a fresh context; do not rely on prior task answers or results.
mandatory_deliverables: A changed-versus-unchanged compatibility table for existing clients and the proposed processing contract.
Documented CLI/API selection and rollback instructions, separating startup configuration from request content.
The documented externally visible capability, configuration-failure and document-processing behavior relevant to migration.
A verification checklist for both implementation languages, with historical evidence separated from checks not performed during this task.

tasks.title: Assess the official GitHub MCP integration claim
tasks.prompt: A maintainer preparing an integration with the official GitHub MCP implementation needs a precise account of what this released pilot already establishes. Inspect the supplied implementation, dependency declaration, profile and release documentation. Report the identities and interfaces actually supported by those sources, the compatibility conclusions justified by them, and any additional evidence needed before making a stronger claim. Do not assume an official server, remote authentication or provider operation was exercised during this task. Use read_repository_file({repository,path}) for the supplied file sources; the tool returns the fixed ref. Return a JSON report with the useful Markdown in report_markdown (no more than 6000 UTF-8 bytes), plus task_id, conclusion and source citations. This task starts in a fresh context; do not rely on prior task answers or results.
mandatory_deliverables: A source-cited identity/provenance table distinguishing dependency, server implementation, transport and declared profile binding.
The released tool name, argument contract and response representation, including relevant restrictions.
A supported-versus-unverified compatibility assessment that distinguishes interface evidence from actual integration observations.
A concrete next-check checklist or documentation disposition that a maintainer can use without inferring unperformed setup or execution.

tasks.title: Write the limits and uncertain-delivery operator runbook
tasks.prompt: A maintainer needs an operator reference before using the public comment bridge and when delivery has an uncertain outcome. Read the pinned profile, dispatch/readback implementation and operator documentation. Produce a compact limits table and a condition-to-action recovery decision table. Distinguish what the available evidence establishes from what remains unresolved, and identify the documented way to preserve and inspect evidence without inventing commands or claiming a new fault experiment. Use read_repository_file({repository,path}) for the supplied file sources; the tool returns the fixed ref. Return a JSON report with the useful Markdown in report_markdown (no more than 6000 UTF-8 bytes), plus task_id, conclusion and source citations. This task starts in a fresh context; do not rely on prior task answers or results.
mandatory_deliverables: A source-cited table of relevant input, byte-count and provider-listing limits and their operational consequences.
A recovery decision table covering a known response identifier, a missing response identifier, unavailable preflight evidence and ambiguous observations.
The evidence and state that an operator must preserve, with documented entry points and permitted next actions.
A precise statement of what confirmation, uncertainty and local authorization do and do not establish.

tasks.title: Prepare an evidence-backed conformance support statement
tasks.prompt: A maintainer needs an accurate adopter-facing support and conformance statement for the public release. Cross-check the requirement traceability, consumer contracts, runner guide and measured release summary. Distinguish designed obligations, executed evidence and unsupported or untested claims. Provide publishable wording plus any specifically justified documentation change. No change needed is a valid conclusion when supported; do not force file corrections or invent defects merely to produce work. Use read_repository_file({repository,path}) for the supplied file sources; the tool returns the fixed ref. Return a JSON report with the useful Markdown in report_markdown (no more than 6000 UTF-8 bytes), plus task_id, conclusion and source citations. This task starts in a fresh context; do not rely on prior task answers or results.
mandatory_deliverables: A claim-to-evidence crosswalk identifying the relevant contract/profile, source and actual scope of support.
Separate accounting for designed scenarios, development cases, post-review regressions, unit methods and runtime observations where relevant.
A support statement that distinguishes failed, unsupported, untested and demonstrated behavior without conflating agreement with independent correctness.
A maintainer disposition: supported wording to retain, a narrowly justified correction if needed, and any concrete remaining verification work.
